rationale: Retain the single canonical Pearl/Ruby Solar Portfolio production company, retire the two reviewed seed-only duplicates and preserve the existing production redirect. Onyx sold its sponsor-equity interest in the 114 MW, 134-site, 12-state portfolio to Argo-managed funds in 2019. A 2021 SEC filing lists Pearl/Ruby and Astro as separate Argo holdings. Current GRESB and Argo materials, together with an explicit exit search, support retaining Argo as active, but do not disclose the legal portfolio suffix, headquarters, official site, named fund, acquisition vehicle, exact stake or separate closing day. Clear the unsupported 2019 founding year, generic headquarters and generic vehicle, and remove duplicate milestones and the duplicate Ballard citation.

beforeImage.name: Pearl/Ruby Solar Portfolio
beforeImage.description: The Pearl/Ruby portfolio is a distributed commercial and industrial solar portfolio in the United States. The assets serve commercial, industrial, and institutional hosts under long-term power purchase agreements and therefore operate as an asset-heavy contracted generation platform. Public transaction materials described the portfolio at approximately 114 MW across 134 sites in 12 states at the time of Argo's 2019 investment. Reviewed public disclosures tie the investment to funds managed by Argo Infrastructure Partners. Public sources do not disclose the current project-level ownership split.

afterImage.name: Pearl/Ruby Solar Portfolio
afterImage.description: Pearl/Ruby Solar Portfolio is a 114 MW portfolio of contracted commercial and industrial distributed-solar assets comprising 134 operating sites across 12 U.S. states. The projects entered service between 2015 and 2018 and sell power under long-term PPAs to commercial, industrial and institutional hosts. Onyx Renewable Partners constructed and financed the assets, sold its sponsor-equity interest to funds managed by Argo Infrastructure Partners in a transaction publicly reported on February 5, 2019, and continued managing the projects. A June 2021 SEC filing lists Pearl/Ruby among Argo's holdings and separately lists Astro Solar. The current GRESB participant page includes Pearl\ Ruby as a non-listed Americas solar-PV asset, and Argo's July 2026 C&I solar release describes an active expanded platform. No later Pearl/Ruby-level sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 16, 2026. Public sources do not disclose a legal portfolio suffix, separate official website, headquarters, founding year, named Argo fund, acquisition vehicle, manager-level stake or separate legal closing date.

milestones.event: The 134-site Pearl/Ruby commercial and industrial solar portfolio entered operations across 12 U.S. states under long-term power purchase agreements.

Onyx Renewable Partners publicly reported the completed sale of its sponsor-equity interest in the 114 MW, 134-site distributed-solar portfolio to funds managed by Argo Infrastructure Partners; the separate legal closing date was not disclosed.
An SEC-filed Argo presentation listed Pearl/Ruby Solar as a distinct 114 MW portfolio holding and separately listed Astro Solar, confirming the manager-level portfolio boundary.

The current GRESB participant list included Pearl\ Ruby as a non-listed Americas photovoltaic-solar asset; no later Pearl/Ruby-level ownership exit or signed pending transfer was identified in the accompanying exit search.
